raj-sales: Quick question on the Dedicated commit we're finalizing — how do overage/autoscale bursts get billed when the burst pool uses a different GPU family (A100 baseline, L4 burst)? :thinking:
amanda-solutions: Short answer: baseline commit billed against the committed SKU/hour. Bursts are billed at the actual GPU SKU/hour used, but we support an equivalence mapping for quoting. We can also apply a capped monthly burst spend if you want a hard limit.
raj-sales: Got it. Need to confirm for customer: will overage show as a separate line item or fold into the monthly invoice? Also need an example calc to share.
amanda-solutions: It shows as separate line items: (1) committed reservation charge, (2) burst/overage usage. Example snippet below I can paste into the quote:
amanda-solutions: ```
Committed: 8 x A100 reserved for 30 days = 8 * 24 * 30 = 5760 A100 GPU-hours
A100 reserved rate = $3.50/hr -> reserved charge = 5760 * 3.50 = $20,160
Burst activity: 120 L4 GPU-hours at $0.60/hr = 120 * 0.60 = $72
If using equivalence mapping (1 L4 = 0.12 A100), billable A100‑equiv hours = 120 * 0.12 = 14.4 -> 14.4 * 3.50 = $50.4
We can choose explicit SKU rates (L4 @ $0.60/hr) or map to A100-equivalent pricing for consistency in the quote.
```
mike-finance: Thanks — finance prefers explicit SKU pricing on the invoice (separate lines) for auditability. Also confirm proration: if commit starts mid-billing-cycle we prorate the reserved charge by days active in the month. Overage is charged at usage during the same period.
raj-sales: Customer asked whether we can offer a soft cap on monthly burst spend so they don't get surprised. Example: cap burst to 150% of commit value or an absolute $ cap. Is that doable?
olivia-se: Yes, we can add a "burst cap" addendum. Two options we typically propose:
olivia-se: 1) % cap: bursts billed up to X% of committed spend, excess require pre-approval.
olivia-se: 2) Hard cap: blocks further burst capacity beyond $Y in a month (autoscale will still queue but flag).
olivia-se: For POC customers we often use % cap at 125–150% to give headroom.
raj-sales: Perfect. Customer prefers % cap. Can we reflect that in the SOW and have legal/finance sign off?
mike-finance: We'll need the exact language. Suggest: 'Burst usage will be billed at list SKU rates. Monthly burst charges will be capped at 150% of the monthly committed reservation charge unless Customer provides prior written approval to exceed.' Legal to approve final phrasing.
sre-ops: Note: capacity for bursts is best-effort across shared pools. If customer requires guaranteed burst capacity we need a different reserved carveout (dedicated burst pool) and different pricing. Put a short note in the SOW: autoscale is not a guaranteed SLA for extra GPUs.
amanda-solutions: Good call. I'll add the SRE note into the SOW draft and create two pricing lines in the quote: (A) committed reservation, (B) burst (capped at 150% by default).
amanda-solutions: I'll also include both billing-display options (explicit SKU lines vs A100-equivalent mapping) so procurement can choose.
raj-sales: Awesome. Can you drop the quote numbers by EOD? Customer wants to sign this week.
amanda-solutions: On it — I'll upload the draft quote + SOW to the shared drive and post link here when done. :thumbsup:

olivia-se: One more practical tip for the customer: recommend enabling prefix caching + token-level batching — it cuts burst spend by reducing tokens sent during peak. I'll add that to the POC runbook.
raj-sales: Great. Thanks everyone — this clears the ask. Waiting for the quote link.
amanda-solutions: Link posted: https://drive.internal.redwood/quotes/DD-2026-045 (draft) — please review.
mike-finance: Reviewing now. If we sign, confirm invoice cadence: monthly in arrears by default, can do net-30 with early-pay credit if needed.
raj-sales: Customer prefers monthly arrears, fine.

raj-sales: Thanks — closing for now. :white_check_mark:
